# Random-matching singlet survival: dimension-free loss witness

Date: 2026-10-29. Status: author derivation, awaiting independent review.
This is a new construction, not an assertion of historical novelty or hardware readiness.

## Operational statement
Let n=2m >=4 spin-1/2 systems, let P be their total-spin-zero projector, and
let d=rank(P)=binom(2m,m)/(m+1). Let N be ANY CPTP map from these n systems
back to the same physical space. No collective-noise model is assumed.
A test consists of:
1. Privately sample a uniform perfect matching M of the n labelled systems.
2. Prepare a singlet on each of its m edges, yielding the pure state |M>.
3. Apply N once, with the same source boundary as the intended storage operation.
4. Measure each of the SAME m edges in the Bell basis. Pass iff EVERY edge
   reports its singlet. Equivalently the passing effect is rho_M=|M><M|.
Let q=1-E_M Tr[rho_M N(rho_M)] be the actual average failure probability.

For every isometry V:C^K -> range(P), use the physical encoder V and the
reset-completed decoder D_V(X)=V* X V + Tr[(I-VV*)X] tau, where tau is any
fixed logical density matrix. Then

    1-F_e(D_V N V) <= (d/K) [(n+2)/(n-1)] q.                 (1)

Here F_e is maximally mixed input entanglement fidelity; notation N V means
rho -> N(V rho V*). In particular K=d gives coefficient (n+2)/(n-1).
Choosing K the largest power of two <=d gives d/K<2 (or =1 when d is a
power of two). The coefficient stays below 2(n+2)/(n-1), irrespective of
Hilbert-space dimension. For K=1 actual logical entanglement infidelity is
zero under the reset-completed decoder, but (1) remains a valid loose bound.

The statement certifies the currently tested map, not a future arbitrary map.
In a conditional sequential experiment the same inequality applies separately
at each actual source-memory history whenever that history defines a CPTP
source input-output map and the current matching is sampled independently.
It is NOT by itself a composable memory-comb or postselected diamond theorem.
Existing sequential guard results require their separate hypotheses.

# Independent matching-survival architecture derivation
2026-10-29. Governing spectral premise remains separately reviewed. No novelty or hardware superiority claim.

Let P be the d-dimensional singlet projector and rho_M=|M><M| the uniform perfect-matching product-singlet ensemble. Assume E rho_M=P/d and its Hilbert–Schmidt operator frame has eigenvalue 1/d on I_P, with all traceless eigenvalues at most lambda/d. For n>=4 the author's candidate is lambda=3/(n+2). This document proves the operational bridge, not that spectral premise.

For arbitrary CPTP source N with Kraus A_a define B_a=P A_a P, alpha_a=Tr(B_a)/d, and leakage l=sum_a||(I-P)A_a P||_HS^2/d. Let F_P=sum_a|alpha_a|^2, the raw entanglement fidelity relative to identity on P. Trace preservation gives sum_a||B_a-alpha_a P||_HS^2/d=1-l-F_P. The actual test prepares |M>, invokes N, and accepts iff every original matched pair measures singlet. This is precisely the rank-one projector rho_M, not a coarse total-spin projector. Therefore

q=1-sum_a E_M |Tr(rho_M B_a)|^2
 >= (1-lambda)(1-F_P)+lambda*l.

Leakage and nonunitality have not been discarded: leakage makes the inequality stronger. If Q is any K-dimensional subcode of P, then

K(1-F_Q)=min_{beta_a} sum_a||(A_a-beta_a I)Q||_HS^2
 <= sum_a||(A_a-alpha_a I)Q||_HS^2
 <= sum_a||(A_a-alpha_a I)P||_HS^2=d(1-F_P).

Here raw F_Q uses the physical output overlap with the same code subspace. Any TP decoder that inverts Q exactly and replaces leakage with a fixed logical state has entanglement fidelity at least F_Q: its added Kraus contributions are nonnegative squares. Consequently its logical Bell loss e satisfies

e <= [d/(K(1-lambda))] q.

Thus the candidate coefficient is C=(d/K)(n+2)/(n-1), including K=d where admissible. n=2 has d=1 and no traceless subspace; the advertised coefficient can be used conservatively but is not its sharp spectral result.

# Independent receiving review of actual logical two-design comparison v9
2026-10-29. Reviewer: review_actual_logical_comparator.

## Disposition
The declared v9 comparison is accepted as a reproducible, conditional-on-one-training-history mathematical fixture. It does not establish hardware performance, training-average yield, historical novelty, or practical superiority after full control and storage costs. The preserved source is unchanged. Additional optimized-weighted and matching comparisons are separate follow-on files, not replacements for v9.

## Actual construction and shared inputs
The program imports exactly the v8 no-reset acquisition/guard fixture. Its fitted frame uses the completed physical-record counters and fixed basis embedding. Both test families use the same learned encoder E, CPTP reset-completed decoder D, final two-dimensional bath state and fixed post-training source U0. The source rule changes at the learning/guard boundary as disclosed in the accepted v8 review; “no reset” is not a claim of unchanged parity-selected source dynamics.

For each of the six logical Pauli eigenstates psi, the test constructs bath Kraus matrices
B = (outket* tensor I) (D_alpha tensor I) U (E psi tensor I) / sqrt(6),
with outket=psi for pass and its normalized orthogonal complement for fail. Summing over every decoder Kraus operator is essential: leakage replacement is included rather than projected away. This is an actual instrument, not a rescaling of a service-error probability. Pass plus fail is trace preserving. For every bath state, the six-state 2-design identity gives the failure effect F=(2/3)W, where W is the nonidentity Pauli service effect. The program checks this full bath-operator identity for U0 and the separately supplied burst unitary, not just one initial bath expectation. The known-generator use of U and sigma is evaluator-only; neither is granted to the physical controller.

The comparator replaces the test CP maps, then executes exactly the same service maps and outer decoder. Its s=0.4, C=1.5 choice gives R=Cs/(1-s)=1, t=6 and b=0, so the prior reviewed accepted-subnormalized soundness bound stays 1/128. The 155 inner services encode 35 payload qubits using the same GF(32) outer code. The cap is500 instead of1400; cap exhaustion aborts and is accounted in both results.
